notes: 18 courses total (6 lower-division + 12 upper-division). Verified: the 'eight upper-division courses in literatures in English' bucket plus one theory course plus three comparative-breadth courses = 12 upper-division. Includes a secondary-language requirement.

buckets.label: Upper-division literatures in English (period coverage)
buckets.note: Eight upper-division literatures-in-English courses, including at least one from each of the four categories: British before 1660, British after 1660, US before 1860, and US after 1860 (four required period courses plus four additional English electives).

buckets.label: Upper-division criticism/theory
buckets.note: One upper-division course in history of criticism or literary/cultural theory: LTTH 110, LTTH 115, or LTCS 100.

buckets.label: Upper-division comparative breadth
buckets.note: One Literatures of the Americas (LTAM), one Literatures of Europe (LTEU), and one additional from LTAF/LTAM/LTEA/LTEU/LTWL.

buckets.label: Secondary-language requirement
buckets.note: At least one course in a secondary language or literature (taught in a language other than English). UCSD Literatures in English requires knowledge of a second language, satisfied by completing the lower-division sequence in an approved second language through its designated terminal lower-division course. This is a proficiency requirement (not a single fixed course) — it can also be met by placement/prior proficiency reaching the same terminal level. Confirmed terminal courses per catalog (LIT-ug.html): French LTFR 2C, German LTGM 2C, Spanish LTSP 2C/2E/3F, Italian LTIT 50, Russian LTRU 2B, Classical Greek LTGK 3, Latin LTLA 3, Hebrew JUDA 3, American Sign Language 1E (Linguistics; subject code LISL, verify). Any of these terminal courses (or equivalent placement) satisfies the requirement; the listed courses are the demonstration endpoints, not an all-of set.
